newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil authorizes 7.14 pct rise in minimum salary.
newsitem.headline: Brazil authorizes 7.14 pct rise in minimum salary.

text.p: Brazil is raising its minimum monthly salary by more than seven percent to 120 reais ($113) effective May 1, Finance Minister Pedro Malan said on Friday.
"The minimum salary, from May onwards, will be 120 reais," Malana said in a statement broadcast on television and radio.
The minimum salary, currently at 112 reais, was last adjusted in May 1996. The new level of 120 reais compares with an initial minimum of 64.79 reais set on July 1, 1994.
The minimum salary, which the Brazilian government is raising by decree, applies as the official base compensation for all Brazilian workers.
A basic basket of goods now cost 114.21 reais, up about 6.8 percent from 106.95 reais in July 1994. With the minimum salary rising 7.14 percent, its actual buying power is climbing, Malan said.
The minimum salary was adjusted with an eye to holding down inflation, rather than correcting past price movements, he said.
"The government recognizes that the increase from the actual 112 reais to 120 reais is small," he said.

"However, this is the amount it can afford at the moment because it is the amount compatible with the weight and impact which the minimum salary has, not on the whole of the Brazilian economy, but on the government accounts," he added.
Malan said five out of 100 registered workers now received the minimum salary, with collective wage negotiations ensuring that even non-qualified workers generally earned more.
